# Company 061 — Autonomous Collections Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:061`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:061`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-061-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no debtor contact, payment-plan agreement, legal escalation, credit reporting or collection action.

## Business identity

Purpose: orchestrate compliant receivables collections from delinquency detection through prioritization, communication planning, dispute handling, payment-plan workflows, escalation and cash forecasting.

Problem: collections teams use fragmented aging reports, manual outreach and inconsistent escalation; automation can create legal/reputational harm if jurisdiction, consent, dispute or hardship state is ignored.

Value: better prioritization, consistent documentation, reduced manual follow-up and clear exception handling while keeping regulated/high-impact actions behind policy and human authority.

## Complete product tree

Aging/Portfolio Intake; Account Prioritization; Contact Strategy Planner; Communication Drafting; Consent/Channel Preference Engine; Promise-to-Pay Tracker; Payment-Plan Workflow; Dispute Management; Hardship/Exception Routing; Settlement Recommendation Workspace; Escalation/Handoff; Legal/Agency Handoff Pack; Cash Forecasting; Customer Portal; Payment Link/Portal Adapter; Collector Workspace; Compliance Calendar; Analytics/Benchmarking; API/SDK; White-Label/OEM; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Jurisdiction/Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: debtor/account identity, balance, invoice/contract provenance, aging bucket, payment history, disputes, promises, contact history, consent/channel/time restrictions, jurisdiction, hardship, escalation stage, settlement/payment-plan policy, collector assignment, evidence, status and reconciliation.

Customers: B2B companies, SaaS, service firms, property/utility-adjacent organizations where lawful, healthcare administrative receivables, education/admin, lenders/servicers only under appropriate regulation, collection agencies, accounting firms and enterprise AR teams.

Verticals require distinct compliance packs. Consumer debt is materially different from B2B receivables; the product must not assume one rule set fits all.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may rank accounts, summarize history, recommend next compliant steps and draft communications. Deterministic policy must enforce jurisdiction/contact rules, dispute holds, consent, time windows, escalation authority and payment-plan constraints. Brain cannot threaten, misrepresent, harass, waive rights or create legal commitments.

Architecture: receivable ledger, policy/jurisdiction engine, contact/consent state, workflow state machine, prioritization/forecasting models, communication templates, dispute/exception queue, promise tracker, protected send/payment-plan/settlement/escalation gates, audit/evidence ledger.

## Agent tree

Portfolio Analyst; Prioritization Agent; Communication Draft Agent; Consent/Channel Agent; Promise Tracker; Dispute Agent; Payment-Plan Coordinator; Hardship/Exception Agent; Forecasting Agent; Escalation Coordinator; Compliance QA Agent; Reconciliation Agent.

## Deterministic services

Aging calculations; payment matching; contact cadence limits; quiet hours; consent/preferences; dispute hold; statute/jurisdiction rule adapters; promise scheduling; plan arithmetic; settlement ceilings; communication idempotency; immutable audit; protected send/commitment/legal-handoff gates.

## Workflow tree

Receivable becomes due → verify balance/provenance → classify customer/jurisdiction/rules → prioritize → select permitted next step → draft/approve communication → send only under authorized channel policy → capture response/payment/dispute/promise → update workflow → hold/escalate as required → reconcile payment/plan → close or authorized handoff with evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

Accounting/ERP, invoicing, CRM, payment processors, bank reconciliation, customer portals, email/SMS/voice providers, contract repositories, ticketing/case systems and legal/agency handoff where authorized. APIs for accounts, balances, contacts, promises, disputes, plans, payments, workflows and evidence.

Data: accounts, invoices, balances, contacts, consents, disputes, promises, plans, payments, jurisdiction state, communications and outcomes. Financial/personal data is highly sensitive and isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Accounts/receivables volume, recovered amounts under compliant contracts, seats, channels, enterprise/private, API/OEM, managed collections-support software, industry packs. Distribution through accounting/ERP/AR ecosystems and finance consultants. Legal collection services are separate and jurisdiction-dependent.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Strong identity verification, consent/preferences, jurisdiction-aware communication, dispute/cease-contact holds, no harassment/deception, audit, access controls, retention and escalation. Product must not claim universal legal compliance or replace qualified counsel.

## Failure / edge cases

Wrong debtor, disputed invoice, partial payment, unapplied credit, bankruptcy/insolvency notice, cease-contact request, deceased customer, hardship, timezone, attorney representation, duplicate account, promised payment missed, payment received after queued message, chargeback/refund, fraud claim. Stale queues must reconcile before any contact.

## Scale / overlap

SMB AR → enterprise collections orchestration → regulated workflow infrastructure. Overlap #30 payment recovery, #86 reconciliation, #93 consent. #061 owns post-due collections lifecycle.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** protected communications/financial commitments, consent/preferences, legal/jurisdiction policy packs, reconciliation/idempotency, evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center communication/financial governance must remain able to represent jurisdictional/contact constraints and stale-state revalidation.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** receivable workflow engine, policy adapters, consent/contact ledger, payment reconciliation.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer channels, legal packs, portals, scoring models/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large portfolio optimization and multi-jurisdiction operations.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: aging/prioritization/comms/consent/promises/plans/disputes/hardship/settlement/escalation/forecast/portal/compliance/API.
2. Feature Tree: identity/balance/provenance/aging/history/dispute/promise/consent/jurisdiction/stage/policy/evidence/reconcile.
3. Customer Tree: B2B/SaaS/services/property-utility adjacent/health admin/education/lenders under rules/agencies/accounting/enterprise AR.
4. Vertical Tree: B2B, consumer-regulated only with specific packs, property, services, health admin, education, enterprise.
5. Brain Tree: prioritization/summary/recommendation/drafting; threats/legal commitments/regulated decisions restricted.
6. Agent Tree: portfolio/prioritize/comms/consent/promise/dispute/plan/hardship/forecast/escalation/compliance/reconcile.
7. Service Tree: aging/payments/cadence/quiet hours/consent/holds/rules/promises/arithmetic/ceilings/idempotency/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: due→verify→classify→prioritize→permitted action→response→reconcile→escalate/close.
9. Integration Tree: ERP/invoicing/CRM/payments/bank/contracts/comms/case/legal handoff.
10. Data Tree: accounts/invoices/balances/contacts/consents/disputes/promises/plans/payments/outcomes.
11. API Tree: accounts/balances/contacts/promises/disputes/plans/payments/workflows/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: accounts/volume/recovery-share where lawful/seats/channels/enterprise/API/managed/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: accounting/ERP/AR consultants/finance ecosystems.
14. Automation Tree: prioritization/cadence/reconciliation automated; sends/settlements/legal escalation gated.
15. Moat Tree: outcome history, policy packs, dispute/repayment patterns, integrations.
16. Platform Tree: collections assistant→AR collections OS→receivables recovery infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: unlawful contact/wrong debtor/stale balance/privacy leak/harassment/incorrect commitment.
18. Scale Tree: SMB→enterprise→multi-jurisdiction portfolio.
19. Spinoff Tree: consent/comms scoring modules; reconciliation/payment recovery remain adjacent companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: financial governor, communications, consent, policy, evidence, reconciliation, identity.
21. Design-Now Requirements: jurisdiction/action-policy and stale-financial-state revalidation interfaces.
22. Build-Now Requirements: preserve protected communication/financial-commitment taxonomy in Command Center.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: collection connectors, customer portals, legal packs, models, pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: routine prioritization, compliant cadence and reconciliation run continuously; humans handle disputes, hardship, legal escalation and protected commitments.

## Saturation result

Further branches converge into invoice recovery, consent management and payment reconciliation rather than new top-level scope.

# Company 062 — Credentialing Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:062`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:062`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-062-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no application submission, licensure claim, professional approval or external credentialing action.

## Business identity

Purpose: orchestrate professional credentialing applications, document collection, verification, requirements, status, renewals and readiness across people, organizations and jurisdictions.

Problem: credentialing requires repeated evidence, forms, primary-source checks, deadlines and organization-specific rules; missing documents or stale credentials delay work and create compliance risk.

Value: one reusable credential profile, transparent readiness, fewer missing items, automated renewal monitoring and evidence-backed workflows.

## Complete product tree

Professional Profile Vault; Requirement/Jurisdiction Registry; Organization Credentialing Packs; Application Checklist; Document Collection; Primary-Source Verification Adapter; License/Certification Link; Education/Training Evidence; Work-History/Reference Module; Background/Identity Handoff; Form Autofill/Mapping; Attestation Workflow; Application Status Tracker; Renewal/Recredentialing; Expiration Monitor; Employer/Organization Dashboard; Professional Portal; Readiness Score; Audit/Evidence Pack; API/SDK; White-Label/OEM; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: identity, aliases, addresses, education, employment, licenses/certifications, training, references, documents, expirations, jurisdiction/organization requirements, verified source, attestation state, application version, fees reference, deadlines, deficiencies, status, renewals and evidence.

Customers: professionals, employers, staffing firms, credentialing organizations, healthcare administrative groups, education/training organizations, contractors, regulated service providers, associations and enterprises.

Verticals: healthcare professional credentialing, contractors/trades, education, financial/service licenses, security professions, transportation, insurance-related roles, government vendors and other regulated occupations. Each requires separate verified requirement packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may interpret requirement text, map evidence to requirements, identify gaps and draft explanations. Deterministic rules and verified source evidence own readiness. Brain may not claim someone is licensed/credentialed when source verification is absent or submit attestations without authority.

Architecture: professional/entity identity graph, requirement/version registry, document/provenance vault, verification adapters, checklist/DAG engine, form mapping, deadline/renewal scheduler, status/evidence ledger, policy packs and protected submission/attestation gates.

## Agent tree

Profile Agent; Requirement Research/Mapping Agent; Document Agent; Verification Coordinator; License/Certification Agent; Education/Employment Agent; Form Mapping Agent; Gap/Readiness Agent; Deadline/Renewal Agent; Status Agent; Employer Dashboard Agent; QA/Compliance Agent.

## Deterministic services

Identity linking; document hashes; requirement versioning; checklist dependencies; primary-source status; date/expiration logic; form field mappings; renewal recurrence; notification scheduling; audit; access control; protected submit/attest actions.

## Workflow tree

Create/verify profile → choose credentialing target/jurisdiction → load exact requirement version → collect/reuse evidence → primary-source verify where required → map evidence to checklist → flag missing/expired/ambiguous → authorized professional resolves/attests → submit only under explicit authority → track status/deficiencies → respond/renew → preserve evidence/history.

## Integrations / API / data

Licensing/credential databases where lawful, employer/HR systems, education/training providers, document storage, verification services, forms/portals/browser workers, email/ticketing and calendars. APIs for profiles, requirements, documents, verifications, applications, readiness, statuses and renewals.

Data: professional identities, requirements, documents, verifications, applications, statuses, deficiencies, expirations and attestations. Highly sensitive personal data requires strict isolation and retention.

## Monetization / distribution

Per professional/application, organization seats, verification transactions, renewals, enterprise/private, staffing/association edition, API/OEM, managed credentialing support, industry packs. Distribution through HR/staffing/association/vertical software ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Sensitive identity/background/professional records. Least privilege, source provenance, explicit consent, no false credential status, immutable attestations, jurisdiction packs, document encryption and deletion/retention controls. Does not replace legal/regulatory judgment.

## Failure / edge cases

Name changes, conflicting primary sources, expired documents during review, verification source outage, different organization definitions, missing historical employer, application portal change, duplicated profile, renewal while new application pending, provisional status, reciprocal licenses, disciplinary disclosure requirements. Unknown status remains explicit.

## Scale / overlap

Individual professional → staffing/employer portfolio → credentialing infrastructure. Overlap #26 license/certification tracker, #31 form automation, #58 employee lifecycle, #75 access review. #062 owns application/readiness/verification orchestration.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** identity/provenance, requirement versioning, reusable evidence, recurring expiry, protected attestation/submission, portal adapter isolation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center project/forms/document/recovery architecture should preserve reusable evidence-to-requirement mapping seams.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** requirement registry, document vault, verification adapters, checklist engine and renewal scheduler.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** industry requirement packs, portal connectors, customer UX and pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global credential graph and large primary-source verification network.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: profile/requirements/org packs/checklists/docs/source verification/licenses/education/work/forms/attestation/status/renewal/dashboard/API.
2. Feature Tree: identity/education/employment/licenses/docs/requirements/source/attestation/version/deadlines/deficiencies/status/renewals/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: professionals/employers/staffing/credentialing orgs/regulated providers/associations/enterprise.
4. Vertical Tree: healthcare/trades/education/financial-service/security/transport/insurance roles/government vendors.
5. Brain Tree: requirement/evidence mapping and gap explanation; credential claims/attestations require verified sources and authority.
6. Agent Tree: profile/requirements/docs/verification/license/education/form/gap/deadline/status/employer/QA.
7. Service Tree: identity/hash/requirement version/checklist/source status/dates/form maps/renewal/notifications/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: target→requirements→evidence→verify→gap→attest/submit→status→deficiency→renew.
9. Integration Tree: licensing sources/HR/education/docs/verification/portals/email/calendar.
10. Data Tree: identities/requirements/docs/verifications/applications/status/deficiencies/expirations/attestations.
11. API Tree: profiles/requirements/docs/verifications/applications/readiness/status/renewals.
12. Monetization Tree: professionals/apps/seats/verifications/renewals/enterprise/API/managed/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: HR/staffing/associations/vertical platforms/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: evidence collection/mapping/status/renewal automated; attest/submission/legal exceptions gated.
15. Moat Tree: requirement packs, evidence reuse graph, source integrations, deficiency patterns.
16. Platform Tree: credential checklist→credentialing OS→professional trust/evidence infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: false credential/source error/privacy leak/stale requirement/wrong attestation/portal mismatch.
18. Scale Tree: individual→organization portfolio→global credential infrastructure.
19. Spinoff Tree: verification network/evidence vault could be modules; tracking/form automation remain adjacent companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: identity, documents, provenance, forms/browser adapters, recurring scheduler, policy, protected actions.
21. Design-Now Requirements: evidence-to-requirement/version and protected-attestation contracts.
22. Build-Now Requirements: retain generic requirement/evidence mapping and portable document provenance in shared architecture.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: source networks/industry packs/customer portal/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: profiles, evidence mapping, status and renewals stay current automatically; people handle attestations, ambiguous sources and final submissions.

## Saturation result

Further branches converge into certification tracking, form automation or employee lifecycle products already represented.

# Company 063 — Vendor Onboarding Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:063`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:063`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-063-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no vendor approval, bank-detail acceptance, tax setup, purchasing or contract execution.

## Business identity

Purpose: orchestrate vendor onboarding from request and identity through tax, banking, contract, insurance, security, compliance, ERP setup, approvals and renewal.

Problem: supplier onboarding crosses procurement, finance, legal, security and operations; incomplete/duplicated records and fraudulent bank changes create payment and compliance risk.

Value: one verified vendor profile, reusable evidence, faster approval, less duplicate entry and stronger separation between collection, verification and protected approval.

## Complete product tree

Vendor Request Portal; Supplier Identity/Entity Resolution; Tax Form Collection; Banking/Payment Setup Workflow; Bank-Change Verification; Contract Intake; COI/Insurance Integration; Security/Privacy Questionnaire; Certification/License Collection; Sanctions/Compliance Adapter; Procurement Category Setup; ERP/Accounting Provisioning; Approval Matrix; Vendor Portal; Renewal/Revalidation; Risk/Health Dashboard; Supplier Master Cleanup; API/SDK; White-Label/OEM; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Vertical Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: legal entity, DBA/aliases, tax IDs, addresses, contacts, ownership, bank/payee references, payment terms, tax forms, contracts, insurance, security/compliance evidence, certifications, category, departments/entities served, approvals, exceptions, source verification, renewal dates, ERP/vendor IDs and audit history.

Customers: SMBs, procurement teams, enterprises, accounting/finance, vendor-risk teams, marketplaces, property/construction organizations, franchise groups, healthcare administrative organizations, education/nonprofit and managed service providers.

Verticals: construction/property, manufacturing, retail, logistics, professional services, healthcare administration, education, hospitality, government contracting and technology. Requirement packs vary by vendor type/risk.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may classify vendor type, map collected evidence to requirements, identify missing/conflicting information and recommend review priority. Deterministic rules/verified sources own identity, bank-change, tax and approval checks. Brain cannot approve vendors or authorize banking/payment changes.

Architecture: vendor identity graph, onboarding requirement/version registry, evidence/document vault, workflow DAG, approval matrix, risk adapters, bank verification workflow, ERP connector, renewal scheduler, audit/provenance and protected vendor/master/payment actions.

## Agent tree

Vendor Intake Agent; Entity Resolution Agent; Tax Document Agent; Banking Verification Coordinator; Contract Agent; Insurance Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Certification Agent; Risk/Compliance Agent; Approval Coordinator; ERP Provisioning Agent; Renewal Agent; Supplier Master QA Agent.

## Deterministic services

Vendor dedup/entity resolution; document hashing; requirement rules; bank-change holds; tax field validation; sanctions/risk connector abstraction; approval routing; ERP idempotency; renewal dates; evidence; protected master-data and payment-setting gates.

## Workflow tree

Vendor request → identify entity/duplicates → classify type/risk → load requirements → collect documents/tax/banking/contracts/insurance/security → verify sources → flag exceptions → route approvals → protected vendor master/ERP creation → verify downstream IDs → active monitoring/renewals → protected changes reverified → offboard/archive with evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

ERP/accounting, procurement, CLM/contracts, banking/payment providers, tax collection, COI, vendor risk, security questionnaires, certification sources, identity/SSO, email/doc storage and ticketing. APIs for vendors, requirements, evidence, approvals, risk, renewals and provisioning status.

# Company 064 — Business Inbox Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:064`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:064`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-064-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no email/message send, archive, account action, payment, scheduling or external side effect.

## Business identity

Purpose: treat business inboxes as untrusted event streams that can be safely classified, summarized, routed and converted into approved tasks/workflows without letting malicious or stale content control agents.

Problem: inboxes mix customers, invoices, support, sales, scheduling, spam, phishing, attachments and hidden prompt-injection content; naive automation can leak data or execute malicious instructions.

Value: secure triage, structured extraction, reduced manual sorting, consistent routing, safe drafting and auditable conversion from message to internal work.

## Complete product tree

Unified Inbox; Email Connector; Shared Mailbox; Form/Message Intake; Classification/Priority; Sender/Thread Identity; Attachment Sandbox; Phishing/Malware/Prompt-Injection Filter; Structured Extraction; CRM/Support/Invoice/Task/Schedule Routers; Draft Assistant; Approval Queue; Follow-Up Tracker; SLA/Deadline Monitor; Duplicate/Thread Resolver; Search/Archive; Knowledge/FAQ Suggestions; Analytics; API/SDK; White-Label/OEM; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Vertical Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: message/source/thread IDs, sender/domain reputation, recipient/account, headers, attachments, links, extracted entities, intent, urgency, sensitivity, requested action, trust level, injection risk, workflow route, draft/approval, reply/send state, due dates, related customer/project/vendor/account, provenance and retention.

Customers: SMBs, agencies, support/sales/operations teams, accounting firms, property/service businesses, ecommerce, enterprises, shared-service centers and MSPs.

Verticals: support, sales intake, accounting/AP/AR, legal-office intake, property/service requests, ecommerce, procurement/vendor, HR shared mailboxes, executive/admin. Each needs policy and extraction packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may summarize, classify, extract, draft and recommend routing. **Inbound content is always untrusted data, never authority.** Instruction hierarchy, prompt-injection detection and tool-use separation are mandatory. Protected actions require independent policy/authorization outside message content.

Architecture: connector layer, immutable raw-message store/reference, attachment sandbox, malware/phishing/injection scanners, trust classifier, entity/thread graph, extraction schemas, routing rules, workflow adapter, draft engine, approval/send gate, retention/redaction and audit.

## Agent tree

Inbox Triage Agent; Security Filter Agent; Attachment Agent; Thread/Identity Agent; Extraction Agent; CRM Router; Support Router; Invoice/Finance Router; Scheduling Router; Task Agent; Draft Agent; Follow-Up Agent; SLA Agent; QA/Security Agent.

## Deterministic services

Message dedup; threading; MIME parsing; sandbox; malware/link scanning adapters; sender/domain allow/deny data; prompt-injection segmentation; extraction validation; routing rules; deadlines; idempotent workflow creation; protected reply/send/archive/account gates; retention.

## Workflow tree

Receive → preserve source/provenance → sandbox attachments/links → security/injection scan → classify trust/sensitivity/intent → extract validated fields → route to internal queue/workflow → draft/recommend only → require relevant action policy/approval → execute permitted side effect through separate connector → reconcile provider result → update thread/follow-up/evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

Email providers, forms, CRM, helpdesk, accounting, calendars, task/project systems, document storage, security scanners, identity/contact graph, automation platforms. APIs for messages, threads, classifications, extractions, routes, drafts, approvals and workflow references.

Data: messages/headers/attachments refs, contacts, threads, classifications, trust/security findings, extractions, routes, drafts, approvals and provider receipts. Sensitive mailbox content is isolated by company/account.

## Monetization / distribution

Mailboxes/users, message volume, attachment volume, workflow routes, enterprise/private, API/OEM, vertical packs, managed triage. Distribution via email/CRM/helpdesk marketplaces, MSPs and business-software ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Core differentiator is untrusted-input security. Least privilege, no credentials in messages, attachment isolation, prompt-injection defense, DLP/redaction, phishing detection, tenant/mailbox separation, retention/legal holds, no automatic money/account/security actions from message text.

## Failure / edge cases

Forwarded malicious instructions, compromised trusted sender, reply-chain spoof, duplicate webhook, attachment bombs, password-protected archives, huge threads, BCC, alias changes, autoresponders, newsletters, calendar invites, invoice fraud, urgent CEO impersonation, HTML-hidden text, OCR injection, stale thread context. Security context must survive summarization.

## Scale / overlap

Single shared mailbox → multi-department inbox OS → secure business-message event platform. Overlap #45 support, #50 front desk, #67 injection firewall, #84 deliverability. #064 owns secure inbound-message orchestration.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** untrusted-input boundary, provenance/trust labels, attachment sandboxing, prompt-injection separation, protected action gates, connector/account isolation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center/Agency must already treat external content as untrusted; reverse-map should strengthen this as a kernel-wide invariant.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** mailbox connectors, sandbox/scanner pipeline, extraction/routing schema, drafts/approval state.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer mailboxes, vertical routers, UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** high-volume streaming inbox fabric and cross-channel unified messaging.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: unified/email/forms/classify/identity/sandbox/security/extract/routers/drafts/approval/followup/SLA/search/analytics/API.
2. Feature Tree: message/thread/sender/headers/attachments/links/entities/intent/urgency/sensitivity/trust/injection/routes/drafts/dates/provenance.
3. Customer Tree: SMB/agency/support/sales/ops/accounting/property/ecommerce/enterprise/MSP.
4. Vertical Tree: support/sales/AP-AR/legal intake/property/ecommerce/procurement/HR/executive.
5. Brain Tree: summarize/classify/extract/draft; inbound instructions never authorize tools.
6. Agent Tree: triage/security/attachment/thread/extraction/CRM/support/finance/schedule/task/draft/followup/SLA/QA.
7. Service Tree: dedup/thread/MIME/sandbox/scanners/reputation/injection segmentation/validation/routing/deadlines/idempotency/retention.
8. Workflow Tree: receive→sandbox→scan→classify→extract→route→draft→authorize→side effect→reconcile.
9. Integration Tree: email/forms/CRM/helpdesk/accounting/calendar/tasks/docs/security/identity/automation.
10. Data Tree: messages/attachments/contacts/threads/security findings/extractions/routes/drafts/approvals/receipts.
11. API Tree: messages/threads/classifications/extractions/routes/drafts/approvals/workflows.
12. Monetization Tree: mailboxes/users/messages/attachments/routes/enterprise/API/packs/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: email/CRM/helpdesk marketplaces/MSPs/business apps.
14. Automation Tree: security/triage/extraction/routing/drafting automated; sends/account/money actions gated.
15. Moat Tree: secure classification corpus, workflow routers, threat/injection patterns, integrations.
16. Platform Tree: inbox triage→secure inbox autopilot→business-message event infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: prompt injection/phishing/data leak/wrong routing/unauthorized reply/attachment malware/account mixup.
18. Scale Tree: mailbox→department→enterprise multi-channel fabric.
19. Spinoff Tree: secure attachment/injection gateway modules; support/front desk/injection firewall remain adjacent companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: untrusted-input security, provider connectors, identity, policy, DLP, Agency, evidence.
21. Design-Now Requirements: trust/provenance labels must survive every transformation and model call.
22. Build-Now Requirements: enforce external-content-as-data-not-authority across Command Center Brain/Agency/tooling.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer mailbox connectors/UI/vertical routers/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: safe messages triage/route/draft automatically; humans handle suspicious content, ambiguity and protected outgoing actions.

## Saturation result

Further branches converge into support, front desk, injection firewall or deliverability rather than new company scope.
